accepted.evidence: Andersen's ah- 'to say' head explicitly compares RV āha and Pali āha and lists the Ashokan third-person perfect āha/āpa series. Turner 1538 ā́ha 'says' lists the same Vedic and Pali word and Prakrit āhaṁsu/āhu; this is the saying verb, not āp- 'water'.

Andersen's separate āpa line on printed p. 141 explicitly says 'for āha, see āha'; the preceding ah- 'to say' paradigm on printed p. 140 gives Udegolam āpa as its 3sg perfect variant. Turner 1538 anchors the āha family.

Andersen prints misibhūta- 'mixed, coupled, united', compares Sanskrit miśrībhūta- and Pali missibhūta-, and explicitly cross-references misa- and hu-. Turner 10135 miśrá includes Ashokan misa- 'mixed'; Turner 9416 bhávati includes Ashokan hoti 'becomes'. Both installed source heads have accepted rank-1 ancestry, so retain the two printed lexical components.
